outline.chapter_title: Supreme Court Fraud Jurisprudence: Ciminelli and Kousisis
outline.description: Provides essential background on two key Supreme Court decisions that define the boundaries of federal fraud liability. Explains Ciminelli's rejection of the right-to-control theory and Kousisis's confirmation of the fraudulent-inducement theory, which are central to resolving whether the indictment sufficiently states an offense.

outline.chapter_title: The Fifth Circuit's Analysis and Holding
outline.description: Details how the Fifth Circuit applied Ciminelli and Kousisis to determine whether the indictment sufficiently alleged a scheme to defraud and intent to defraud. Explains why the court concluded the indictment properly stated securities fraud charges under the fraudulent-inducement theory.
